items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I played with Eli a while and then I'd play with Grant Moore a while

ctx.x: And naturally we had jam sessions and things afterwards, when guys like Eddie Inge and Jimmy Dudley and those guys used to jam. There was a very fine saxophone player in Milwaukee that never did leave there, only to go to Minneapolis, named Earl Keith. He played great alto and great saxophone. He reminded you of guys like Charlie Parker, really great. But he never left, he stayed out that way.

But Jimmy Dudley left and went to the Cotton Pickers. First he went to Billy Minor in Detroit and then he went to the Cotton Pickers. So anyway, we played around Milwaukee that winter and then we finally -- then I finally left there and we went to Minneapolis to play for the Stecker Brothers. And in that interim I had this -- I was playing from one band -- I played with Eli a while and then I'd play with Grant Moore a while, except for the time we got snowbound up there. And after switching from band to band and…

Then I had -- I was always itchy to go someplace so I wrote a fellow up in Toledo had a band called Frank Terry's Chicago Nightengales, I think it was. And I wrote them a letter and they sent for me and I went up there as his musical director and arranger and saxophone player. And this is where I met Art Tatum. Art Tatum was -- I was living on
